name: Cable Rope Triceps Pushdown
nameDa: Tricepspres ned i kabel med reb
movementPattern: Elbow extension - upper arms at sides
grip: Neutral grip with one rope knot in each hand, palms facing each other.
description: Push a cable rope downward by straightening the elbows, spreading the rope ends slightly outward at the bottom to maximize triceps peak contraction.
setup: Attach a two-strand flexible rope to a high cable pulley and select the appropriate pin setting.
Face the pulley and grasp the rope ends with a neutral grip (palms facing inward).
Step back slightly, establish a stable hip-width stance with a subtle forward torso hinge.
Tuck elbows tight to your ribs with forearms angled upward around 90 degrees.
instructions: Straighten your elbows to push the rope downward toward your thighs, keeping your upper arms stationary at your sides.
As you approach full extension, spread the rope ends outward beside your hips and actively squeeze the triceps.
Pause under control at the bottom lockout without locking joints forcefully.
Allow the elbows to flex smoothly to return the rope to the 90-degree starting position, resisting the cable pull.
cues: Keep elbows pinned at your sides.
Spread the rope at the bottom.
commonMistakes: Allowing the elbows to drift forward and backward, using shoulder momentum.
Rounding the upper back or leaning excessively over the rope.
Failing to spread the rope at the bottom, reducing lateral head recruitment.

logging.example: Cable stack pin set to 22.5 kg: record 22.5 kg on that machine.
logging.note: Record selected stack weight, rope attachment, and pulley station. Pulley ratios and cable friction vary across manufacturers.

variantNote: Standing cable pushdown using a flexible rope attachment, allowing forearm pronation and rope flare at peak contraction.
